prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, from small molecules that recruit ubiquitin ligases to the molecular identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type glue degraders

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: a single prize part for targeted protein degradation, credited to Crews, Deshaies and Handa. I moved to it from perovskites after the opening ballots, and nothing in round 1 has pushed me back. It is the only shortlisted candidate that all eight members ranked, and four of us independently arrive at the same trio, which is not a support count I rely on but does show the three names map onto separable, checkable contributions: the heterobifunctional concept and its demonstration in cells (Crews, Deshaies), and the identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target (Handa). From my own field, the part I weigh most is that the mechanism is carried by determined structures. Ternary-complex crystal structures of degrader, ligase and target show what induced proximity means at atomic resolution, and the cereblon-thalidomide structures explain the glue branch. A citation that says induced proximity, with PROTACs and cereblon glues as the two demonstrations of it, is a single achievement in the sense the chair asks about, and I would write it that way and not as two parts. Approved cereblon-directed drugs already exist, so the molecular-glue half is clinically validated even though no PROTAC is approved yet.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is approved, and the PROTAC design rules are still largely empirical, so the heterobifunctional half rests on concept and clinical-stage evidence more than on a finished modality. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex crystallography are what made the field rational, and Sakamoto shares authorship of the first PROTAC paper with Crews and Deshaies; a trio that omits both is defensible but contested, and I cannot rule out that experts would put Ciulli ahead of Handa. Whether the work is new chemistry or pharmacology and chemical biology is a fair question that I answer only partly: the reaction being directed is biological, but the molecule, the design principle and the structural explanation are chemical. If the committee judges that recognition should wait for clinical proof, perovskites and the lipid nanoparticle case are the strongest alternatives I can defend.

responses.point: Chabes asks whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one achievement or two, and how the three places should be allocated among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto.
responses.response: I treat them as one achievement, induced proximity to a ubiquitin ligase, with two demonstrations: designed bifunctional molecules and the discovery that thalidomide-type drugs act as monovalent glues through cereblon. The structural evidence is common to both, because the ternary and cereblon-drug complexes show the same logic of a small molecule remodelling a protein surface. That is why I keep Handa over Ciulli for the third place: Handa's work explains an approved drug class and is a distinct, datable step, whereas Ciulli's contribution refines the design of the PROTAC branch. I accept your point that the pairing is a judgement and not a natural fit, and that is why the citation should name induced proximity and not a single molecule type.

responses.point: Aili argues that ionizable lipid nanoparticles are molecular design and self-assembly that solved the delivery problem, and complement the 2023 Medicine prize, with Cullis, Madden and Anderson as the trio.
responses.response: I take the complementarity argument seriously, and B019 is now my first alternative. Where I still differ is on how cleanly the decisive step can be credited. Sparr and you disagree on the third name, and the committee has not settled whether the Vancouver encapsulation chemistry or the lipidoid screening line was decisive, so any trio leaves out Hope, MacLachlan or Langer, or Anderson. I also want evidence that endosomal escape through pKa tuning and non-bilayer phase behaviour is demonstrated by structure or phase data and not inferred from efficacy. Degradation has a comparable attribution problem, but the three names there correspond to separate steps, and its mechanism is supported by determined structures.

responses.point: Sparr says the decisive credit in lipid nanoparticles lies with Cullis, Madden and Hope, and that phase behaviour explains encapsulation and release, but concedes she may overweight the phase explanation and that Anderson would replace Hope if lipid-library design was decisive.
responses.response: That candour is useful, and the phase-behaviour account is the part of B019 I find most convincing as chemistry, since packing parameters and phase diagrams can be measured. My concern is that the account explains why the particles work but leaves open why the Vancouver trio and not MacLachlan or Langer should carry the citation, and you say yourself that the answer could flip to Anderson. A trio that depends on how the committee resolves that question is less secure than one where the three names are separable. I would not oppose B019 if the committee resolves the attribution question clearly, but I do not think it has been resolved in round 1.

responses.point: Somfai argues that Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is mature, cleanly attributed to Buchwald and Hartwig, and arguably overdue after the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize.
responses.response: I agree that the attribution is the tidiest on the shortlist and that the mechanism is well understood, and I have no doubt about maturity. My hesitation is the same as yours, that after 2010 it reads as a new nucleophile on an established logic, whereas induced proximity is a new modality that changes what a small molecule can do. I do not think the 2010 prize disqualifies B016, and I take the point that bench-level impact is easy to verify. But a prize in 2026 that the Academy must defend to the wider public is easier to defend with a concept that opens new questions than with an extension of one, so it stays behind B056 for me.

responses.point: Brzezinski says the three B056 names map onto distinct steps, but that Handa's cereblon work and the PROTAC concept are two lines that a citation must hold together without implying a single discovery.
responses.response: I agree the wording matters, and I have rewritten my citation so that it says induced proximity, with the PROTAC concept and the cereblon identification named as separate contributions, and does not suggest one discovery. On your perovskite remark from round 1, I accept that stability, lead content and a six-name credit make that case harder than B056, and I no longer put it first for those reasons. I would add one safeguard. If the committee wants Ciulli included, that should displace Handa only if the experts show the VHL and ternary-complex work was a decisive enabling step and not a refinement, since displacing Handa would weaken the glue half of the citation.

responses.point: Linke prefers nanopore sensing with Deamer, Akeson and Bayley as a mature capability with one transparent principle, and concedes thin support and the Branton and Kasianowicz omission.
responses.response: I agree on the transparency of the principle and on maturity, and as an electron crystallographer I value methods that let a community see what it could not see before. My difficulty is the same as yours: the trio leaves out Branton and Kasianowicz, who demonstrated translocation in 1996, and I cannot see a rule that makes the cut principled and not arbitrary. There is also the chemistry-or-instrumentation question you raised yourself. On your chair question about what would move me, evidence that the credit set can be justified without those omissions would be needed, and I do not see it from the material available.

uncertainties: Whether Handa or Ciulli should hold the third place, and whether Sakamoto's role in the first PROTAC paper makes the trio vulnerable to a priority challenge.
Whether the committee accepts recognition of induced proximity before any PROTAC is approved, given that cereblon-directed glue drugs are approved.

Whether the cereblon-directed glue mechanism is established structurally well enough to carry half of the citation, which I believe it is but have not checked against the primary structural literature.
Whether degradation will be treated as new chemistry or as pharmacology and chemical biology.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted achievement or credited name. I remain a Stockholm University colleague of the Secretary, Peter Brzezinski, who also supports B056, but we have no collaboration with any credited person and no recusal is needed. No change from round 1.
